elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 as rendered still binds Ono and its Affiliates: "During the first twelve (12) months of the term of this Agreement, neither Ono or its Affiliates ... shall Commercialize in the Ono Territory ... [a Competing Product]". A narrowed covenant on Customer remains, so the preferred (no restriction at all) position is not achieved; the drafter targeted the fallback, not the preferred level.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: The covenant is confined to the pre-existing defined term "Competing Product", i.e. a product whose active pharmaceutical ingredient is an agent of the specified redacted class other than the two named licensed compounds (Binimetinib / Encorafenib). It is product-class specific and tied to the licensed molecules, not an open "any competing business" formulation; the definition was left unchanged by the redline. Caveat: the class descriptors are redacted ([ * ]) in the source, so breadth cannot be read on the face of the document, but the definitional anchor to Binimetinib and Encorafenib is express.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: The temporal anchor was replaced with "During the first twelve (12) months of the term of this Agreement", and the entire post-termination tail ("in the event that Array terminates ... prior to the [ * ] anniversary of the date such termination takes effect") has been deleted. No obligation survives expiry or termination.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "During the first twelve (12) months of the term of this Agreement" — an express 12-month cap replacing the redacted open-ended period; the conforming change in the Ono-breach sentence ("during such twelve (12) month period") keeps the termination trigger co-extensive with the capped covenant.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: "The foregoing restriction shall not apply to Ono's or its Affiliates' internal Development activities ..." — an express carve-out using the Agreement's defined term Development.

"... or to any Competing Product acquired by Ono or its Affiliates in connection with a merger, acquisition or similar transaction." — express acquisition carve-out covering acquired Competing Products.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: named/defined Competing Product scope retained, covenant confined to the term, capped at twelve months, with express internal-Development and acquisition carve-outs. Preferred is not met because a restriction on Customer survives, which is consistent with the claimed 'deviation' status and the chosen fallback target.

Edits are confined to the checklist: temporal anchor narrowed, post-termination tail deleted, two carve-outs inserted, and the Ono-breach termination trigger conformed to the new twelve-month window so it does not float on a deleted period. No survival tail, expense language, extra remedies or unrelated boilerplate was added.

Favourable retained language survives: the mutual structure (Array and its Controlled Affiliates also bound in-term), the royalty-termination consequence if Array Commercializes a Competing Product, and the unchanged Competing Product and compound-class definitions.

Repair recommended (not fatal): the retained sentence "If during the [ * ], Array Commercializes a Competing Product in the Ono Territory, the royalty payment period shall terminate" still uses the redacted period reference while the parallel Ono sentence was conformed to "such twelve (12) month period". If "[ * ]" was an anaphoric reference to the deleted opening period rather than an independently defined term, this leaves a dangling anchor — confirm the definition or conform the reference expressly.

Note for the drafter: shortening the shared anchor also shortens Array's in-term restriction from the original redacted period to twelve months, giving up some Customer-favourable protection. This is an unavoidable by-product of editing a single mutual temporal anchor (splitting the obligations would add more operative text), so it is not treated as a minimality failure, but Ono may prefer to preserve Array's longer restriction by bifurcating the covenant.

Comment is accurate and matches the operative text: it states the term-limitation, deletion of the post-termination tail, and the two carve-outs, and confirms the Competing Product definition is unchanged; nothing material is merely promised in the comment.
